findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The two storage racks inside of the walk in cooler still contained visible mold on the surfaces.  A presence of mold inside of any cold holding equipment poses several health risks to food items, as well as food contact surfaces. There is also a sticky trap stored near a holding rack where fried chicken is dumped after being fried. The PIC mentioned that Plunkett’s, the facility’s pest control company, placed the trap in that specific area. Discussed that insect traps are to never be stored in a manner where it can contaminate food or food contact surfaces.

(B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Several food items such as but not limited to milk and potato salad were observed to not be date marked in the mini cooler. PIC noted that the milk was recently opened. Ensure that any TCS food stored in house more than 24 hours should be date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

Hand sanitizer is not the same as soap and cannot be used as a substitute.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 1) Open gallon of milk in the prep area reach-in cooler was without a date mark. PIC stated milk was just opened within the last couple of days. Benefit of doubt was given for product, and milk was dated and kept for use.
2) Egg rounds (cooked/cooled on-site), precooked sausage patties, and deli meat were observed with date marks of 9/13 in the top holding compartment of the breakfast sandwich prep cooler. Open package of deli ham was observed with a label that was not legible and worn from moisture. All products appeared to be fresh and were said to be prepared and/or opened at the start of the week. Proper date marks were provided during inspection. 
Date marking educational handout was provided for reference. Ensure proper date marking for all required products.
Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Crock of gravy was observed with an internal temperature of 57F-60F in the chicken walk-in cooler. PIC noted the crock was removed from hot holding unit around 10:30am and put in the cooler around 12pm. Best practices were discussed for quick chilling process. Gravy was placed in an ice bath and stirred to help product reach 41F within the remaining ~2hrs of time frame for cooling. Educational handout for cooling was provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs. One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Handles of manual faucet were touched after handwashing was completed to shut off faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and employee was advised on use of paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet after hands were dried to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

Hands shall also be washed upon entering the food service/prep area and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

Solutions were made earlier in the morning and needed to be changed. Fresh solutions at 200ppm were provided. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently depending on use.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Popcorn scoop and storage tray were soiled with food debris. Popcorn was not currently available for service and machine was off. PIC noted popcorn is made about every 3 days. Ensure scoop and all equipment used for popcorn service are cleaned after use. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not TCS food shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred or at least up to every 24hrs.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Chili in hot holding unit at condiment counter was observed with an internal temperate of 127F-130F. Product was said to be heated in the microwave to 170F around 9am. Hot holding unit was set at #5 and adjusted to a higher number. Water in hot holding well was observed at 164F with inspector’s probe thermometer. Chili was to be reheated to 165F/above prior to placing product back in hot holding unit at condiment counter. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 1) Open gallon of milk in the prep area reach-in cooler and open deli meats in the top holding area of the prep cooler were without date marks. Both products were said to be opened two days prior on Monday. Products were properly dated and kept for use.
2) Cooked egg rounds were observed with a date mark of 2/1 in the top holding area of the prep cooler. PIC noted the eggs were just cooked the day prior. Cooled portion of cooked eggs with date mark of 2/21 was observed in the walk-in cooler. Proper date mark was provided for working supply of cooked eggs. 
3) Containers with open packages of hotdogs in the back storage cooler had date marks with an open date of 2/19 and use by date of 3/4. PIC was advised on 7 day time frame for use unless product/food safety information is available to indicate products are good for longer than 7 days once original packaging is opened. Open hotdogs should be served or discarded by 2/25 based on prep date.
Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-502.13 Dispensing tubes of bulk creamer and half & half bags were not cut at an angle. Ensure tubes are cut at an angle at a length of ~1inch. 
The bulk dairy container dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1) Shelving in the walk-in cooler was soiled with general buildup and mold on some section.
2) Shelving used for storage of fryer oil and bulk potatoes was soiled with powder and grease.
Clean shelving throughout the facility as needed to eliminate buildup of mold, grease and other debris.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Hanwashing sink in prep area was loose and pulling away from the wall. Provide repairs to firmly attach the handwashing sink to the wall and seal the sink to wall juncture with caulk.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink next to the 3 part sink to be out of paper towels at the start of the inspection. Ensure each hand sink is stocked with paper towels. The hand sink was stocked with paper towels during the inspection. 
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulking next to the hand sink to be falling off, cracking and not connected to the wall. Ensure caulking is replaced so the surface behind the sink is smooth and easily cleanable. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: Observed the scoop used for flour to be a cup without a handle. Ensure a scoop with a handle is used to prevent possible contamination. 
(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the area behind the soda nozzles to be soiled with soda and mildew debris. Ensure this area is cleaned frequently so it is maintained clean. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Observed an employee beverage without a lid and straw placed above the prep cooler. Beverages must be kept in a designated area, be below the food prep or storage surface, and/or have a lid and straw. The employee placed a lid and straw on the beverage and moved it from above the prep cooler. 
(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed a cleaning part for the fryer sitting in the hand sink at the start of the inspection. The part was moved during the inspection. Hand sinks may only be used for handwashing only. 
(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
